title: AI medical scribe: what it does and how to test one safely
description: How an AI medical scribe turns a doctor visit into a chart note, what a published health-system study found, and how to test one with privacy rules in mind.
summary: An AI medical scribe listens to a patient visit, with consent, and drafts the clinical note. The clinician reads, fixes and signs it. The goal is less time typing notes, especially after hours.

example.input: A recorded 15-minute visit about knee pain, including the exam and the plan to order an X-ray.
example.output: A draft note with the history, exam findings, assessment and plan sections filled in, for the clinician to edit and sign.

howToTest: Run a pilot with a small group of clinicians who volunteer, and track the same measures for a similar group without the tool.
Measure time in notes per visit, after-hours charting time, and the share of notes closed the same day, before and after.
Have a second clinician compare 30 drafts to the recording and count missing facts and invented facts.
Ask patients if they were told about the recording and whether they agreed.
Check where the audio and text are stored, who can see them and how long they are kept.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy in almost every case. Privacy contracts, chart system connections and clinical safety checks are heavy work.
buyVsBuild.build: Build only if you are a large health system with a research team and a need the products do not meet.

watchOuts: A vendor that handles patient information for you is usually a HIPAA business associate. HHS says you need a written business associate agreement before sharing that information.
The clinician stays responsible for the note. A draft with an invented finding is a patient safety problem.
Published results come from specific sites and willing clinicians. Yours may differ.
Obtain patient consent to record in line with your state's rules, which this page does not cover.

sources.name: JAMA Network Open: Clinician Experiences With Ambient Scribe Technology (Feb 2025)
sources.what: A study of 46 clinicians in which mean time in notes per appointment fell from 10.3 to 8.2 minutes after ambient scribing, a 15.2% change.

sources.name: HHS: Business Associates
sources.what: Explains that a covered entity may share protected health information with a business associate only with satisfactory assurances in a written agreement.
